On journeys: Takbir on high ground when returning from Hajj, Umrah or a campaign, not reaching home at night, hastening home, entering houses by doors, and joining prayers when hurrying.
The Prophet usually set out on Thursdays, Tabuk included; he set out after Zuhr at Medina, five days before Dhul Qa'da ended for Hajj, and in Ramadan, fasting until Kadid.
Companions ride double: Anas behind Abu Talha, and Usama behind the Prophet on a donkey and on his camel at the Conquest, when he entered and prayed in the Ka'bah.
If people knew what the Prophet knew, none would travel alone at night; he sped on open ground, delayed Maghrib to join Isha when hurrying, and urged travellers home quickly.
Boys meet the returning Prophet, who says 'we return repentant', is aided by Abu Talha when his camel slips with Safiya, and prays two rak'at in the mosque.
Travellers should not return to their families at night before wives can groom; the Prophet asked newly married Jabir why not a virgin, urging him to seek children.
Travel is a kind of torment, keeping one from sleep and food, so when one's business is done, one should hurry back to one's family.
The Prophet shared his mount: Usama rode behind him on a donkey, and at Mecca he took boys of Bani Abdul Muttalib, Qutham and Al-Fadl, one before and one behind.
